correctness.rationale: Exact facet projections, bivariate Gaussian absolute-product integration and sign-overlap binomial counting establish the mean and second-moment identities. Exact even sign moments, a fourth-order uniform Taylor remainder, a Hoeffding tail bound and a Stirling gamma-ratio expansion rigorously yield \(d^3\operatorname{Var}(B_d)\to1/(3\pi)\). 132 standalone finite diagnostics include vertex-hull comparisons; they supplement but do not prove the uniform theorem.

originality.rationale: The derived object is the \((d-1)\)-volume of a cross-polytope projected onto a Haar-random hyperplane, rather than its line width or an extremal projection volume. The analytic binomial second moment and the sharp \(d^{-3}\) variance coefficient were not implied by the investigated source statements. Priority uncertainty remains for earlier general brightness-covariance literature.
residual_risks: A previously published general covariance identity for brightness of polytopes might contain the finite formula as a specialization without naming the cross-polytope.
Independent historical-priority verification, including older integral-geometric literature not indexed in the searches, remains outstanding.

value.rationale: Hyperplane brightness governs the geometric growth of the hull of a translated convex body. The all-dimensional moment law and strictly positive sharp cubic variance-decay coefficient reveal cancellation of constant, first and second order terms under random orientation; this is a structurally motivated asymptotic distinction not captured by extremal projection-volume inequalities.
